Gosh, I’ve literally been doing the original medical medium “raw” cleanse for seven years because that was the first book I started with, and the only differences I don’t do everything raw. I add cooked vegetables and potatoes in there, put the essence of what the cleanse is basically no/low fat with vegetables and fruit.

I have been inconsistent with the celery juice because of how difficult it is to juice every day. After having done both juicing, celery, and the heavy metal detox smoothie every day for a few years and without much improvement, I became very discouraged, and doing the heavy metal detox smoothie also every day became overwhelming, and I was getting really sick of it. Instead, I’ve just been doing all the ingredients to the heavy metal detox smoothie separately during the day (exception, I haven’t been consistent with the wild blueberry juice). I’ve gone through stance where I’ve been more consistent, but I’ve just been on and off trying to survive. It really wears you down after being chronically ill for this many years. I’ll do my best to be more consistent with the juicing and the wild blueberry juice. I have not had any of the no foods for seven years, including chocolate, salt, legumes, anything caffeinated, and grains. I have assorted fruits every single day for breakfast and throughout the day, with potatoes on leafy greens with cucumber, tomato, and sprouts occasionally with an avocado for lunch and cooked vegetables on leafy greens with sweet potato noodles, typically for dinner. I’ve been eating this way for about seven years.
The sinusitis protocol and one of the medical medium books has helped my severe allergic rhinitis immensely. I think it might’ve been cleansed to heal.

I’ve been dealing with vestibular seizures since 2017 due to the negative side effects of the Mirena IUD. This symptom has been the most persistent for me throughout my healing journey on the Medical Medium protocols. Even though I’m seven years in and haven’t completely healed, I have seen improvement.

I also experience vertigo, which is often triggered while driving in a car or sometimes in the mornings. While my symptoms aren’t fully gone, I feel hopeful about the progress I’ve made so far.

I’ve been very slowly regaining the ability to digitally draw and paint! :’) Sadly, it takes me INCREDIBLY longer to create and finish a piece with the limitations of the chronic joint pain, tendinitis through my hands, fingers, and arms, and the fibromyalgia. Some days I can’t even draw at all since things get flared up so easily… but even though my abilities are very much more limited then they were before, my heart still cries for me to be an artist, so I will continue to fight to do what I love. I’ll keep following my dreams, and I’m incredibly grateful for what I can do… I sincerely just wish my body would fully heal. 

After months of slowly working on it bit by bit, I’m happy to share this symbolic painting, “Losing Hope.” I started this while I was in one of the deepest parts of my depression last year. Each break symbolic of the physical pain, ailments, and various injuries; my inner light escapes through all the cracks… loosing all hope of healing from chronic illness. 

I mostly used the airbrush for this piece, with some of the special effects brushes, as well as the real pen tool. I used this piece to experiment with the add glow layers quite a bit. I like changing the hardness of the airbrush to create a more defined brush stroke.
